scope: Binding for Alpha 0.1 implementation. An Alpha-scope decision does not promote itself to canon; where a decision is deliberately narrowed to Alpha, the narrowing is stated.

decisions.decision: Every participating player has exactly one match-team assignment, North or South. The assignment is total and exclusive: no player is unassigned and no player holds more than one.
decisions.alpha_scope: Admin/debug assignment only. Automatic team formation, balancing, queueing and party handling are out of scope for Alpha 0.1.
implementation_consequences: PlayerData gains an authoritative team field, as match-scoped state rather than a persistent player property.
Contributions.capitalize(worksiteId, team) currently takes a bare String; it should consume the authoritative team type once one exists.
Team assignment is cleared by match reset, per ALPHA-D2.
not_decided: how teams are formed outside Alpha
whether team is ever persistent across matches

decisions.decision: Each match operates on a disposable, restorable instance of the frozen Consolidative Alpha world. Reset returns the world to its pristine Alpha template and clears all match-scoped plugin and player state.
decisions.explicitly_rejected: Piecemeal block rollback. Reset is not defined as undoing individual world edits.
implementation_consequences: The Alpha world becomes a TEMPLATE plus a per-match INSTANCE. Loading a match and resetting a match are then the same mechanism: unload the instance, copy the template, load it. This merges audit items P0.2 and P0.7 into one instance-lifecycle component.
The template lives at artifacts/worldgen/alpha-0.1/consolidative-alpha and must be treated as read-only in practice.
Match-scoped plugin state to clear: team assignment, match state, renewable population, Route designations, Worksite state, infra mode.

Player progression state is match-scoped for Alpha and is therefore cleared. This follows from 'all match-scoped plugin/player state' and is recorded explicitly so the implementation does not have to infer it.
Paper cannot replace a loaded world in place, so the instance must be unloaded before the template is copied over it.
Disk cost is roughly 28 MB per instance; instances are disposable and should not be committed.
not_decided: whether any player state survives a match in later versions
how many instances may exist at once

decisions.decision: A team wins when the opposing team has no remaining living participating players while that team's Aether Fountain is disabled.
decisions.canon_reference: objectives.md:233 - superseded for Alpha by this decision; the Fountain-to-victory transition is now specified for Alpha 0.1.
decisions.fountain_semantics: Fountain disable is not itself victory. It disables that team's ability to respawn. Players already alive remain active and must subsequently be eliminated.
terminal_sequence: eliminate all surviving enemy participating players
decisions.alpha_scope: Fountain disable is irreversible for the remainder of the match. Repair and reactivation remain unresolved and must not be invented now.
decisions.still_unresolved: The prerequisite/exposure relationship between Pillager Outpost, Nether Bastion, End Tower and Aether Fountain. Do not canonize an exposure rule merely to implement Alpha lifecycle testing; debug/admin controls may force Fountain availability and disable state.
decisions.implementation_rule: Implement the real victory predicate even though Alpha is solo-tested. Debug/admin tooling may create or force the state needed to exercise the predicate; it must not replace the actual victory rule with a solo-only win button.

decisions.provenance: Not a new decision. This records an already-established mechanic that the Alpha implementation notes had not recognized, and which an earlier Alpha implementation had approximated as a plain restoration field.
decisions.decision: Death with a functioning friendly Aether Fountain returns the player to that Fountain immediately, retaining ordinary inventory under the existing KeepInventory model, at approximately 1 Health and 1 Hunger. Health and Hunger then RECONSTRUCT at fixed absolute rates while the player remains at the Fountain. The player may leave voluntarily at any point, including before fully reconstructed. A living player who returns to their functioning friendly Fountain uses the same free reconstruction.
decisions.rates: Fixed absolute rates. NOT percentages of maximum and NOT level-scaled. It follows that raising Health/Hunger maxima lengthens full reconstruction rather than leaving it constant, so Capacity carries a cost as well as a benefit.
nonfunctioning_fountain: A player already reconstructing remains ALIVE with their current partial Health/Hunger and their normal maxima. The Fountain falling neither kills nor diminishes anyone.
Subsequent deaths cannot respawn or reconstruct and are permanent.
decisions.feeds: ALPHA-D3: Fountain disabled -> respawns cease -> existing survivors remain -> subsequent deaths permanently eliminate them -> eliminate all survivors for victory.
decisions.saturation: Out of scope. Current authority specifies Health and Hunger only; reconstructed Hunger is ordinary unsaturated Hunger and drains normally once the player leaves. Do not add saturation reconstruction unless separately established.
decisions.alpha_scope: Exact Health/sec and Hunger/sec values, the arrival values, and the Fountain radius remain unresolved balance parameters and are NON-CANON ALPHA FIXTURES in config (features.fountainRegen). Alpha also continues to treat Fountain disablement as irreversible per ALPHA-D3.
decisions.preserved_distinction: The broader design distinguishes temporary Fountain obstruction/repair from permanent physical destruction. Alpha's irreversible disablement is a lifecycle SIMPLIFICATION of that distinction, not a replacement for it; the distinction is not to be rewritten out of the broader design.
still_unresolved: obstruction/repair vs permanent destruction as distinct Fountain states outside Alpha
whether reconstruction interacts with combat (e.g. interruption on damage)

still_open_after_these_decisions: Fountain exposure/prerequisite relationship with Outpost, Bastion and Tower (P1); must not be invented for lifecycle testing
Fountain repair and reactivation (P1); irreversible for Alpha 0.1
respawn destination (P1); Recall.java:83 records the recall destination as unresolved
implementation_hold: LIFTED 20 September 2026. The P0 pass proceeds in dependency order.
confirmations: Player progression and levels are match-scoped and reset between matches.
The pristine-template world-instance lifecycle is authoritative for Alpha reset.
An instance must be unloaded before restoration or replacement. This is an implementation constraint, not a game mechanic.
